## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Trump Demands China and Russia Block Iranian Weapons, Threatens Consequences

President Trump said on July 25 that Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin both pledged not to supply weapons to Iran, while he warned that any involvement would be "very bad" for both countries. Simultaneously, Trump stated Iran is showing its "most serious" commitment yet in ongoing negotiations, though he signaled the US remained "locked and loaded" for military strikes if diplomacy fails. The US also sanctioned six people and 12 firms—including entities in China and Hong Kong—for supporting Iran's ballistic missile program.

**Why it matters.** This crystallizes escalation risk around Iran's military program and the fragility of the negotiation framework. For someone tracking geopolitics with quant and India exposure, this directly shapes near-term asset volatility—oil prices spike on war risk, defense spending surges, and financial stress on Chinese and Russian equities if confrontation deepens. Iran's technical talks with the US on Strait of Hormuz access (running parallel to these warnings) directly impact India's energy security calculus. The great-power choreography here—Xi's assurance, Putin's assurance, Trump's trust-but-verify posture—signals a deal that could shatter on miscalculation. If Iran escalates or any party backs away from pledges, crude prices and India's import costs move sharply.

**Action.** Watch oil futures for volatility around any Iran-US negotiation breakdown. Monitor statements from Chinese and Russian energy companies on Iranian contracts as a signal of actual compliance versus rhetoric. Track the Security Council's expected vote on Iran sanctions renewal. If you consult on supply chain or energy risk, recalibrate India's crude procurement strategy and geopolitical hedging around this narrowing window.

*Sources: [[Trump trusts China, Russia not to arm Iran, warns of consequences](https://www.chinatechnews.com/2026/07/25/126210-trump-trusts-china-russia-not-to-arm-iran-warns-of-consequences)]([Trump trusts China, Russia not to arm Iran, warns of consequences](https://www.chinatechnews.com/2026/07/25/126210-trump-trusts-china-russia-not-to-arm-iran-warns-of-consequences)) · [[Trump warns China and Russia against Iran war involvement](https://chinaglobalsouth.com/2026/07/25/trump-warns-china-russia-iran-weapons-pledge/)]([Trump warns China and Russia against Iran war involvement](https://chinaglobalsouth.com/2026/07/25/trump-warns-china-russia-iran-weapons-pledge/)) · [[Trump maintains that China, Russia are staying out of Iran war](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jul/24/trump-maintains-china-russia-staying-iran-war-citing-relationship-xi-putin/)]([Trump maintains that China, Russia are staying out of Iran war](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jul/24/trump-maintains-china-russia-staying-iran-war-citing-relationship-xi-putin/))*

### US Central Command Deploys to Lebanon as Iran-US Strait of Hormuz Talks Begin

A US Central Command delegation arrived in Lebanon on July 25 to implement an agreement ending hostilities between Israel, Hezbollah, and supporting actors. The ceasefire implementation coincides with Iran-US technical talks in Doha, Qatar based on a 14-point memorandum of understanding, where negotiators are establishing protocols for Strait of Hormuz access and security. The US stated it will not return to military action in the strait unless necessary, signaling a preference for rules-based transit.

**Why it matters.** This deployment represents a potential circuit-breaker on Middle East escalation, but its fragility matters enormously for India. The Strait of Hormuz carries roughly one-third of global seaborne oil; for India, it's the critical transit route for both crude imports and strategic positioning. A failed ceasefire or any Hezbollah-Israel flare-up explodes oil prices and shipping costs instantly. For quant or consulting work, this is the macro event reshaping energy markets and supply chain hedging in real-time. The 14-point MOU signals both US and Iran want deescalation, but implementation in a fractious region with proxy actors historically fails—any Iranian escalation (ballistic missile tests, drone strikes, naval posturing) breaks the deal and sends oil north of $120 per barrel.

**Action.** Subscribe to Security Council Report to track Lebanon implementation; watch for Israeli or Iranian statements that break the agreement terms. Monitor Strait shipping rates via Bloomberg or comparable indices—spikes signal market stress. If advising on India-focused quant models or energy-related portfolios, recalibrate tail risk on oil shock and Strait disruption. This is a high-volatility period that hasn't fully priced in the risk of ceasefire collapse.

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### AMD Bets $5 Billion on Anthropic, Deploys 50,000 MI450x to Oracle — Infrastructure War Accelerates

AMD announced July 23, 2026, that it will invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic and supply 2 gigawatts of MI450 inference chips starting H1 2027. Separately, AMD will deploy 50,000 MI450x accelerators across Oracle data centers beginning H2 2026. Alongside these deals, AMD unveiled Helios server racks as a Nvidia H100 rival and formally launched its Venice CPU for data centers.

**Why it matters.** This signals a structural shift in the inference infrastructure market. For two years, Nvidia owned both training and inference; AMD is now fighting for inference dominance by committing volume and capital to a top lab. If Anthropic actually deploys 2GW of MI450s starting next year, that's real capacity that changes the ROI calculus for running Claude at scale. The Oracle deal proves AMD can compete in the volume game, not just niche play. For teams building production agentic systems, this means multi-vendor AI chip options will exist within 12 months—allowing you to negotiate from a position of actual competition rather than Nvidia's duopoly pricing.

**Action.** If you are provisioning inference infrastructure before Q4 2026, spec out both MI450x and H100 costs; AMD's commitment to Anthropic means MI450 driver support and software stability will improve materially. Watch AMD's Advancing AI 2026 detailed specifications for actual memory bandwidth, latency, and power envelope—the Helios rack specs will tell you whether MI450 can match Nvidia's inference density.

*Sources: [[AMD expected to launch next generation of AI infrastructure to challenge Nvidia](https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/07/23/amd-expected-to-launch-next-generation-of-ai-infrastructure-to-challenge-nvidia)]([AMD expected to launch next generation of AI infrastructure to challenge Nvidia](https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/07/23/amd-expected-to-launch-next-generation-of-ai-infrastructure-to-challenge-nvidia)) · [[AMD and Meta Redefine the AI Landscape with Massive 6-Gigawatt Infrastructure Pact](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/marketminute-2026-2-26-amd-and-meta-redefine-the-ai-landscape-with-massive-6-gigawatt-infrastructure-pact)]([AMD and Meta Redefine the AI Landscape with Massive 6-Gigawatt Infrastructure Pact](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/marketminute-2026-2-26-amd-and-meta-redefine-the-ai-landscape-with-massive-6-gigawatt-infrastructure-pact)) · [[What to expect at AMD Advancing AI 2026](https://www.itpro.com/infrastructure/what-to-expect-at-amd-advancing-ai-2026)]([What to expect at AMD Advancing AI 2026](https://www.itpro.com/infrastructure/what-to-expect-at-amd-advancing-ai-2026))*

### Meta Ships Muse Spark 1.1 — 1M-Token Agentic Model, Paid API Now in Public Preview

Meta announced Muse Spark 1.1, a natively agentic 1-million-token-context model, via Mark Zuckerberg on July 2026. The model is now available through Meta's first-ever paid developer API in public preview. Muse Spark 1.1 supports long-context reasoning and tool-calling patterns required for multi-step autonomous systems.

**Why it matters.** This is the first time Meta is charging developers directly for frontier-model API access—a signal that Llama's open-weight era does not preclude a premium closed offering for production workloads. The 1M token window matters concretely: you can pass entire codebases, long conversation histories, or video transcripts (with appropriate embeddings) in a single request, eliminating context windowing complexity in agent orchestration. For teams building autonomous systems, this means a non-OpenAI, non-Anthropic option with the engineering resources of Meta behind it, reducing single-vendor risk on inference.

**Action.** Test Muse Spark 1.1 for your longest-context agentic tasks—especially retrieval-augmented generation patterns over large documents or multi-step planning loops where context reuse is expensive. Compare latency and token cost to Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on the same benchmark prompts. Review Meta's API docs for tool-calling semantics to understand whether calling patterns differ from OpenAI/Anthropic conventions.

*Sources: [[July 2026 AI Releases: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta AI — ThursdAI](https://thursdai.news/releases/2026-07)]([July 2026 AI Releases: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta AI — ThursdAI](https://thursdai.news/releases/2026-07)) · [[AI Updates Today (July 2026) – Latest AI Model Releases](https://llm-stats.com/llm-updates)]([AI Updates Today (July 2026) – Latest AI Model Releases](https://llm-stats.com/llm-updates)) · [[Best AI Models of July 2026: Ranked by Use Case, Benchmarks & Price](https://www.buildfastwithai.com/blogs/best-ai-models-july-2026-ranked)]([Best AI Models of July 2026: Ranked by Use Case, Benchmarks & Price](https://www.buildfastwithai.com/blogs/best-ai-models-july-2026-ranked))*

## 🇮🇳 India

### HCLTech and Sarvam AI to build ₹14,257 crore sovereign AI data centre in Odisha

HCLTech signed an MoU on July 24, 2026, with Sarvam AI and the Government of Odisha to establish India's first full-stack AI Data Center at the Odisha Sovereign AI Park. The project carries a capital outlay of ₹14,257 crore, including financial assistance from the state government. The facility will combine HCLTech's infrastructure capabilities with Sarvam's indigenous foundation models to deliver sector-specific AI applications for government and enterprise customers.

**Why it matters.** For AI engineers in Hyderabad and across India building LLMs, inference systems, or AI applications, this signals a critical shift from cloud-dependent compute to domestic infrastructure. The "sovereign AI" framing indicates India is prioritizing alternatives to US cloud providers for sensitive workloads. Companies relying on AWS or Azure may face pressure to migrate to Indian infrastructure; engineers building inference or fine-tuning systems should expect that sovereign compute will become a compliance requirement for government contracts within 18-24 months.

**Action.** Track the Odisha Sovereign AI Park's infrastructure specifications when published (GPU provisioning, bandwidth, cooling). Watch for government contracts migrating off US cloud. If building AI products for Indian government or regulated sectors, understand the sovereign compute requirement now—it will reshape RFPs and technical requirements for government-facing AI startups.

*Sources: [[HCLTech Press Release](https://www.hcltech.com/press-releases/hcltech-announces-ai-data-center-bhubaneswar-partnership-sarvam-and-government)]([HCLTech Press Release](https://www.hcltech.com/press-releases/hcltech-announces-ai-data-center-bhubaneswar-partnership-sarvam-and-government)) · [[Business Standard - Investment Details](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/hcltech-ai-data-centre-odisha-sarvam-rs-14257-crore-investment-126072400775_1.html)]([Business Standard - Investment Details](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/hcltech-ai-data-centre-odisha-sarvam-rs-14257-crore-investment-126072400775_1.html)) · [[CXO Today - Partnership Context](https://cxotoday.com/hardware/hcltech-sarvam-ai-and-odisha-join-forces-to-build-new-ai-data-center/)]([CXO Today - Partnership Context](https://cxotoday.com/hardware/hcltech-sarvam-ai-and-odisha-join-forces-to-build-new-ai-data-center/))*

### Investor capital rotates away from AI-only companies toward manufacturing and aerospace

In the week ending July 25, 2026, Indian startups raised $209 million across 18 deals, with manufacturing, aerospace, enterprise software, and healthtech emerging as the dominant funding themes. This marks a sharp shift from the previous two weeks when AI companies dominated capital deployment. The rotation comes after Emergent (AI infrastructure) and Udaan (logistics) drew $130 million and $116 million respectively in earlier July rounds.

**Why it matters.** For AI engineers considering startup trajectory and fundraising, this signals investor skepticism toward pure-play AI companies without proven unit economics or clear paths to margin. VCs are now favoring companies that apply AI to hard manufacturing problems (robotics, quality control, supply chain) or infrastructure (aerospace, enterprise tools) rather than foundation models or AI-as-a-service plays. If you're pitching an AI startup, investors want application moats first, not model capability alone.

**Action.** Review the TICE News funding tracker for which manufacturing, aerospace, and enterprise AI companies closed rounds in this week (Yotta Data Services, Mowito, Blurgs). For founders: study their positioning—they led with real-world problem (autonomous robots, supply chain) not model capability. For engineers: if recruiting into AI startups, check whether the startup has a defensible applications layer, not just a model or fine-tuning service.

*Sources: [[TICE News - Manufacturing and DeepTech Funding Week](https://www.tice.news/tice-trending/india-startup-funding-manufacturing-deeptech-july-25-2026-12195825)]([TICE News - Manufacturing and DeepTech Funding Week](https://www.tice.news/tice-trending/india-startup-funding-manufacturing-deeptech-july-25-2026-12195825)) · [[Tracxn - Funding Tracker](https://tracxn.com/d/geographies/india/__ujYf3QI9FSnpS3x-zJCSwnay2nENQhm1kAN-U8-6Kfg)]([Tracxn - Funding Tracker](https://tracxn.com/d/geographies/india/__ujYf3QI9FSnpS3x-zJCSwnay2nENQhm1kAN-U8-6Kfg)) · [[Industrial Front - Weekly Breakdown](https://industrialfront.com/indian-startups-raise-219-million-in-a-single-week-as-ai-and-deep-tech-dominate-july-2026-deals/)]([Industrial Front - Weekly Breakdown](https://industrialfront.com/indian-startups-raise-219-million-in-a-single-week-as-ai-and-deep-tech-dominate-july-2026-deals/))*

## 🇮🇳 Indian Stocks

### GANDHAR (NSE): +20.0% on record Q1 earnings, dividend announcement

Gandhar Oil Refinery shares surged ₹47.23 to ₹283.42 on July 23, 2026, hitting the upper circuit +20.0% as the refinery announced Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹192 crore against ₹28 crore in Q1 FY26 (638% YoY growth). Volume swelled to 12.5 million shares worth ₹349 crore traded. The company simultaneously declared an interim dividend of ₹2.00 per equity share with a July 31 record date.

**Why it matters.** A 638% profit surge on controlled revenue of ₹1,731.93 crore reflects pricing power in the white oils segment during an inflationary crude cycle—exactly the opposite of what Reliance and Bharat Petroleum face on fuel cracks. EBITDA margins swung to 16.27% (from 5.83% in Q4 FY26), signaling operational leverage and potential for sustained returns if crude holds above $95. For IT talent in Hyderabad, this is a reminder that commodity refining in India remains highly cyclical and catalyzes sharp, rapid repricing when macro sentiment shifts.

**Action.** Check the BSE/NSE filing dated July 23, 2026 for the board-approved Q1 results and dividend resolution. Watch the August earnings call transcript for management commentary on the US $2/bbl crack spread outlook and capex plans—the stock typically re-rates on any guidance reset for Q2-Q3 crude dynamics. Key support sits at ₹265 (previous resistance); resistance at ₹300 (52-week high hit on July 24).

*Sources: [[Gandhar Oil Refinery Board Clears Q1 Results, Interim Dividend and Governance Changes - TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/gandhar-oil-refinery-board-clears-q1-results-interim-dividend-and-governance-changes)]([Gandhar Oil Refinery Board Clears Q1 Results, Interim Dividend and Governance Changes - TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/gandhar-oil-refinery-board-clears-q1-results-interim-dividend-and-governance-changes)) · [[Gandhar Oil Refinery shares rally 20% to hit upper circuit following strong earnings - Upstox](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/gandhar-oil-refinery-shares-rally-20-to-hit-upper-circuit-following-strong-earnings-check-all-q1-numbers/article-197425/)]([Gandhar Oil Refinery shares rally 20% to hit upper circuit following strong earnings - Upstox](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/gandhar-oil-refinery-shares-rally-20-to-hit-upper-circuit-following-strong-earnings-check-all-q1-numbers/article-197425/)) · [[Gandhar Oil Refinery hits the roof after Q1 PAT zooms 689% YoY - Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/gandhar-oil-refinery-hits-the-roof-after-q1-pat-zooms-689-yoy-126072300269_1.html)]([Gandhar Oil Refinery hits the roof after Q1 PAT zooms 689% YoY - Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/gandhar-oil-refinery-hits-the-roof-after-q1-pat-zooms-689-yoy-126072300269_1.html))*

### HCLTECH (NSE): +1.88% on Q1 record bookings, 20% profit growth

HCL Technologies closed July 24, 2026 at ₹1,268.10, up ₹23.40 (+1.88%) as the market re-rated the software exporter on Q1 FY27 earnings announced July 13. Consolidated net profit expanded ₹781 crore year-over-year to ₹4,624 crore (+20.32%), while revenue climbed ₹4,230 crore to ₹34,579 crore (+13.94% YoY). The stock bounced 24% from its July 1 intra-month low, on record Q1 net new bookings of $2,407 million—the highest opening quarter booking total in the company's 30-year history.

**Why it matters.** Indian IT services are in a demand rotation: HCLTech's record bookings amid a tepid 1-4% FY27 revenue guidance (constant currency) tells you clients are re-engaging (capex thaw in US/EU), but deal velocity remains geographically bifurcated. The ₹12 interim dividend suggests management confidence in cash conversion despite the Jaspersoft $240 million acquisition (completed July 1). For engineers tracking rupee strength—INR weakness actually supports TCS/Infosys/HCL FY27 guidance beats. Sector tailwind: IT hiring paused in 2024; wage inflation has peaked; margin expansion is now the vector.

**Action.** Read HCLTech's Q1 FY27 investor presentation (released July 13 on their IR portal) for deal pipeline granularity by geography and practice. The FY27 revenue guidance of 1-4% (CC) vs. street expect ~3.5% is a key watch—if Q2 bookings cool, downside resets to ₹1,200. Key resistance at ₹1,300; watch for any analyst upgrade on margin expansion.

*Sources: [[HCLTech Q1 FY27 Profit rises 20% YoY to Rs 4,624 crore; announces Rs 12/share interim dividend - BusinessToday](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/hcltech-q1-fy27-profit-rises-20-yoy-to-rs-4624-crore-announces-rs-12share-interim-dividend-542630-2026-07-13)]([HCLTech Q1 FY27 Profit rises 20% YoY to Rs 4,624 crore; announces Rs 12/share interim dividend - BusinessToday](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/hcltech-q1-fy27-profit-rises-20-yoy-to-rs-4624-crore-announces-rs-12share-interim-dividend-542630-2026-07-13)) · [[HCLTech Results: Quarterly Results Analysis - INDmoney](https://www.indmoney.com/blog/stocks/hcltech-results-beat-or-miss)]([HCLTech Results: Quarterly Results Analysis - INDmoney](https://www.indmoney.com/blog/stocks/hcltech-results-beat-or-miss)) · [[HCL Tech rallies 24% from July low; hits 3-month high on huge volume - Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/hcl-tech-rallies-24-from-july-low-hits-3-month-high-on-huge-volume-126072400257_1.html)]([HCL Tech rallies 24% from July low; hits 3-month high on huge volume - Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/hcl-tech-rallies-24-from-july-low-hits-3-month-high-on-huge-volume-126072400257_1.html))*

## 💹 Global Stocks

### TSLA (NASDAQ): -14.5% on Q2 earnings miss as operating profit collapses 57% on AI spending surge

Tesla closed at $319.69, down 14.52% on July 23 after reporting Q2 operating income of just $398 million, missing implied expectations by $1.3 billion. Operating margin crashed to 1.4% from 4.1% a year ago as operating expenses jumped 47% to $4.35 billion, driven by artificial intelligence and robotics research. Volume hit 114.2 million shares, 131% above the three-month average of 49.4 million, as short sellers booked $4.1–4.3 billion in single-day profits.

**Why it matters.** Tesla's margin implosion signals that even the most capital-efficient automaker cannot escape the AI capex arms race that has gripped Big Tech. The company posted negative free cash flow of $1.09 billion—its first cash burn in two years—and capex surged 142% to $5.79 billion on autonomy. For India's auto and semiconductor ecosystem, the read-across is stark: sustained AI R&D spending will erode near-term profitability for tech and hard-tech names regardless of revenue growth, pressuring emerging-market valuations if rates stay elevated.

**Action.** Read the Q2 10-Q filing on SEC Edgar for capex breakdown across autonomy, supercomputing, and manufacturing. The July 23 earnings call transcript details management's FY26 capex guidance; focus on comments around Full Self Driving and Tesla Bot spending. Key technical level: the $280–290 range, where prior support failed; watch for a retest of that zone or a stabilization above $310 to gauge buying interest.

*Sources: [[The Motley Fool: Tesla Stock Crashes on Earnings Miss](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/07/23/stock-market-today-july-23-tesla-stock-crashes-on-earnings-miss-and-rising-ai-spending/)]([The Motley Fool: Tesla Stock Crashes on Earnings Miss](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/07/23/stock-market-today-july-23-tesla-stock-crashes-on-earnings-miss-and-rising-ai-spending/)) · [[Gurus Focus: Tesla Major Selloff](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8977413/tesla-tsla-faces-major-selloff-after-earnings-report-misses-expectations)]([Gurus Focus: Tesla Major Selloff](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8977413/tesla-tsla-faces-major-selloff-after-earnings-report-misses-expectations)) · [[Yahoo Finance: Tesla Q2 2026 Report](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/tesla-tsla-stock-trades-down-175631788.html)]([Yahoo Finance: Tesla Q2 2026 Report](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/tesla-tsla-stock-trades-down-175631788.html))*

### GOOGL (NASDAQ): -7.1% despite earnings beat as capex shock turns free cash flow negative for first time

Alphabet slid to $319.88, down 7.13% on July 23 after announcing Q2 capital expenditure of $44.9 billion—double the year-ago $22.4 billion—and raising full-year 2026 capex guidance from $180–190 billion to $195–205 billion. Revenue beat expectations at $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year, and Cloud revenue surged 82% to $12.5 billion, but the capex shock overwhelmed the positive. Free cash flow collapsed to negative $5.9 billion, the first negative quarter in Alphabet's publicly traded history, compared to positive $10.4 billion in Q2 2025.

**Why it matters.** Alphabet's capex-driven FCF deterioration marks a structural shift in the mega-cap AI playbook: hyperscalers are choosing growth in AI infrastructure over near-term shareholder returns. The parent of Google Cloud's 82% YoY growth signals real competitive win versus AWS, but the $100 billion plus annual capex commitment signals that FCF accretion will be deferred for years. For investors in India's IT consulting and semiconductor packaging (Amkor, HCL, Infosys), the implication is sustained long-cycle capex demand from hyperscalers but compressed returns on deployed capital across the entire stack.

**Action.** Review the Q2 10-Q for capex allocation by geography and infrastructure tier (data center, power, connectivity). The earnings call (July 22 after-hours) includes guidance on 2027 capex trajectory and FCF recovery timeline. Key level: $310 support, which if broken, could trigger retesting of the $290–300 range; watch for institutional rotation into lower-leverage mega-caps like UNP or MCD.

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### Zetwerk Closes $52M Pre-IPO Round as India's Manufacturing Unicorn Races to Public Markets

Manufacturing software platform Zetwerk raised $52 million in a pre-IPO funding round backed by Bharat Value Fund, Pantomath Group, and HNI investors on July 25, 2026. The round comes weeks after SEBI granted the company observation letter for its primary IPO on July 10, which targets ₹4,200 crore ($450 million) at a $4 billion valuation. Zetwerk's momentum signals strong investor appetite for deep manufacturing infrastructure as the company moves toward listing.

**Why it matters.** Zetwerk's closing pre-IPO round captures a broader shift in Indian venture capital away from AI hype and toward proven B2B builders solving hard operational problems. The $52 million alone represented nearly one-fourth of all capital deployed in Indian startups the week of July 25—a signal that mature companies with demonstrated unit economics and revenue traction now command investor focus over early-stage bets. For founders in manufacturing, enterprise software, and aerospace, this validates the playbook: build boring, build deep, build for complexity.

**Action.** Track Zetwerk's IPO prospectus filing and roadshow. Follow Bharat Value Fund's thesis on manufacturing consolidation in India—the fund's backing of Zetwerk signals what sectors it expects to scale over the next 18 months. Monitor other pre-IPO activity in this cohort: Veriqus, Qore, and other manufacturing and enterprise software plays preparing public debuts.

### Indian VCs Pivot Hard: Manufacturing and DeepTech Displace AI as Top Investment Themes

Indian startups raised $209 million across 44 funding rounds in the week ending July 25, 2026, marking a 44 percent decline from the previous week but reflecting a dramatic rotation in investor thesis. Manufacturing, aerospace, enterprise software, and healthtech captured the majority of capital, while AI startups—which dominated earlier in July—dropped out of top-funded positions. The shift signals that venture investors are now favoring companies with proven business models and clear path to profitability over speculative plays.

**Why it matters.** This pivot exposes a maturation cycle in Indian venture: founders and LPs are moving past the AI narrative gold rush toward sectors where execution and unit economics matter. Manufacturing startups like Zetwerk and Qore are proving that India can build capital-efficient solutions for the world's supply chain. The messaging to founders is blunt: build revenue, build margins, build something nobody else can do cheaply. This also reflects global sentiment—Series A and later rounds are flowing to companies solving regulated, mission-critical problems where AI is a feature, not the exit.

### Tour de France 2026 concludes in Paris as Pogačar dominates three-week campaign

Janez Pogačar crossed the finish line in Paris on July 26 after 21 stages spanning 3,500 kilometers, capping a dominant three-week campaign that began July 4 in Barcelona. Pogačar entered the final stage with a four-minute lead over Belgium's Remco Evenepoel, having controlled the race through the Alps and Pyrenees. The concluding stage followed the traditional procession into the French capital, cementing one of cycling's most prestigious victories and broadcasting to an estimated 3.5 billion viewers across 200 territories.

**Why it matters.** The Tour de France is the world's second-most watched sporting event after the World Cup, yet its distribution model reveals deep fractures in sports media globally. European broadcasters dominate coverage while African and Southeast Asian markets pay premium rates for rights or go dark entirely. Pogačar's dominance—and the race's routing through Slovenia and Eastern Europe—signals how streaming platforms are beginning to fragment what was once unified continental viewership. This year's record prize money and athlete compensation also reflect how professional cycling is chasing younger audiences through social media, creating competing attention economies versus traditional broadcast windows.

**Action.** Track whether platforms prioritize short-form social clips over live broadcast exclusivity in their Tour coverage—this determines whether 2027 sees a further shift to influencer-driven sports narratives or a reversion to traditional media gatekeeping.

### Africa Women's Cup of Nations kicks off with 16-team expansion and record $2M prize pool

Algeria faced Senegal at 18:00 local time on July 26 as the TotalEnergies CAF Women's Africa Cup of Nations opened in Rabat, Morocco, marking the tournament's historic expansion to 16 participating nations for the first time. Host Morocco followed against Kenya at 21:00 the same evening. The 34-match tournament runs through August 16, offering competing African federations a record $2 million prize pool and direct qualification paths to the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil—stakes that have nearly tripled over the last tournament cycle.

**Why it matters.** Women's sports investment in Africa has remained fragmented across satellite, cable, and streaming—but this expansion signals a consolidation moment. Morocco hosting a third consecutive edition, the expanded field, and raised prize money reflect broadcaster confidence in African women's football audiences. This is a measurable shift in where global sports capital is moving: traditional men's football viewership in Africa is plateauing, but women's tournaments are outpacing audience projections. The tournament's staging across five Moroccan venues also tests whether centralized infrastructure and unified streaming rights can crack the African sports distribution problem that has plagued the continent's media market for two decades.

**Action.** Monitor which platforms secure exclusive streaming rights across African regions and whether clips proliferate on TikTok/Instagram before official broadcast—early adoption patterns here will forecast where women's sports viewership consolidates by 2028.
